Very strong evidence in R-learner and CF; critical marker of nutritional status.
Exceptional R-learner gain; reflects neurological status.
Strong UR score and consistent CF support; reflects patient-reported fatigue.
Significant gain in R-learner; strong indicator of acute clinical status.
High UR magnitude and consistent CF support; marks skeletal burden.

Highest interaction magnitude among chemotherapy agents.

reduction_tradeoffs: Consolidating renal and blood pressure measurements may lose granular distinction between systolic and diastolic effects or eGFR vs. serum creatinine.
Grouping lung diseases assumes a shared causal mechanism for the 'presence' of pulmonary pathology, potentially losing specific COPD vs. interstitial disease signals.
summary: Consolidation focused on removing measurement redundancies (e.g., creatinine, weight, and lung disease descriptors) while retaining high-fidelity markers of renal and cardiovascular health. Confounders were selected based on a strict requirement for empirical evidence in both treatment and outcome models. Modifier representatives were prioritized by the consistency and magnitude of effect evidence across Causal Forest, R-learner, and interaction models, emphasizing biological markers (NLR, Albumin) and critical clinical states (Bone/Brain metastases, performance status).
